_status: RULED - not applied. Three readings await Sam's confirmation (see to_confirm).

1_seed_from_authorities.rule: Where CCN or C-ID publishes a subject code for a discipline's courses the canonical Common SUBJ follows the authority (as shaped by rule 3); the CSR mints its own only where neither has one. The seed records canonical_source in {ccn, c-id, csr}.

3_shape.sam: My gut says use CCN if available; if not, stay with 4-characters and add a CID chip with the verbatim CID code showing; eliminate hyphens.
3_shape.rule: canonical_subj4 stays ^[A-Z]{4}$. Use the CCN code when one exists (all are four letters). Otherwise use the C-ID code only when it is exactly four letters with no hyphen; otherwise keep the CSR's four-letter code and show the C-ID chip with the verbatim C-ID code. No hyphen ever enters a canonical code.
3_shape.consequence: The seed invariant, the id parsers, the fold and the tests that pin four letters are unchanged; the chip is a data field plus a display.

19_c_id_chip.rule: Wherever a canonical code differs from the authority's code, the CSR tab, the CCR tab and SkyView show a chip carrying the verbatim C-ID code(s): a word label ('C-ID'), muted CO blue, one chip per discipline to start and per identity once members are classified. CCN codes never need a chip because they are the canonical code.
